title.zh: 卷三十六 列傳第三十: 始興王叔陵 新安王伯固
title.en: Volume 36: Chen Shuling, Prince of Shixing; Chen Bogu, Prince of Xin'an
title.raw: 卷三十六 列傳第三十: 始興王叔陵 新安王伯固 Volume 36: Chen Shuling, Prince of Shixing; Chen Bogu, Prince of Xin'an

sentences.zh: 陳書卷三十六

translations.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 36
translations.idiomatic: Book of Chen, Volume 36

sentences.zh: 列傳第三十

translations.literal: Biographies 30
translations.idiomatic: Biography 30

sentences.zh: 始興王叔陵 新安王伯固

translations.literal: Prince of Shixing Chen Shuling; Prince of Xin'an Chen Bogu
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shixing Chen Shuling; Prince of Xin'an Chen Bogu

sentences.zh: 始興王叔陵

translations.literal: Prince of Shixing Chen Shuling
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shixing Chen Shuling

sentences.zh: 始興王叔陵字子嵩，高宗之第二子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Shixing Chen Shuling, styled Zisong, was the second son of Emperor Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shixing Chen Shuling, styled Zisong, was Emperor Gaozong's second son.

sentences.zh: 梁承聖中，高宗在江陵為直閤將軍，而叔陵生焉。

translations.literal: In the Chengsheng era of Liang, Emperor Gaozong was at Jiangling as direct-gate general, and Shuling was born there.
translations.idiomatic: During Liang's Chengsheng reign, Emperor Gaozong was at Jiangling as direct-gate general when Shuling was born.

sentences.zh: 江陵陷，高宗遷關右，叔陵留于穰城。

translations.literal: When Jiangling fell, Emperor Gaozong removed to Guanzhong; Shuling remained at Rangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangling fell, Emperor Gaozong withdrew to Guanzhong while Shuling stayed behind at Rangcheng.

sentences.zh: 高宗之還也，以後主及叔陵為質。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong returned, the Last Ruler and Shuling were left as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: On Emperor Gaozong's return, the Last Ruler and Shuling were held as hostages.

sentences.zh: 天嘉三年，隨後主還朝，封康樂侯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianchen, he followed the Last Ruler back to court, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Kangle with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianchen year 3 he followed the Last Ruler home to court and was made Marquis of Kangle with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 叔陵少機辯，徇聲名，彊梁無所推屈。

translations.literal: Shuling in youth was quick-witted and disputatious, pursued reputation, and was overbearing—none could make him yield.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Shuling was sharp and argumentative, hungry for fame, and so overbearing that no one could stand up to him.

sentences.zh: 光大元年，除中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangda, he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangda year 1 he was made vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二年，出為持節、都督江州諸軍事、南中郎將、江州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year, he went out as credential-bearing, commander of all military affairs in Jiang province, southern central-guard general, and inspector of Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he went out bearing the staff, as commander of Jiang military affairs, southern central-guard general, and inspector of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 太建元年，封始興郡王，奉昭烈王祀。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taijian, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shixing to maintain the cult of Prince Zhaolie.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 1 he was made Prince of Shixing to carry on the sacrifices to Prince Zhaolie.

sentences.zh: 進授使持節、都督江郢晉三州諸軍事、軍師將軍，刺史如故。

translations.literal: He was further given the credential staff, command of all military affairs in Jiang, Ying, and Jin provinces, and the post of army mentor general; his inspectorate was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was further granted the credential staff, command over Jiang, Ying, and Jin, and the rank of army mentor general while keeping the inspectorate.

sentences.zh: 叔陵時年十六，政自己出，僚佐莫預焉。

translations.literal: Shuling was then sixteen; government issued from himself alone, and his staff had no part in it.
translations.idiomatic: Shuling was then sixteen; policy came only from him, and his aides were shut out.

sentences.zh: 性嚴刻，部下懾憚。

translations.literal: By nature he was harsh and severe; his subordinates were awed and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: He was harsh by nature, and his subordinates lived in dread.

sentences.zh: 諸公子姪及罷縣令長，皆逼令事己。

translations.literal: The various princes' sons and nephews and dismissed county magistrates and prefects were all forced to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial nephews and dismissed county and prefectural heads alike were forced into his service.

sentences.zh: 豫章內史錢法成詣府進謁，即配其子季卿將領馬仗，季卿慚恥，不時至，叔陵大怒，侵辱法成，法成憤怨自縊而死。

translations.literal: Yuzhang inner administrator Qian Facheng came to the mansion to pay his respects; Shuling at once assigned Facheng's son Jiqing to lead horse equipage; Jiqing, ashamed, did not come in good time; Shuling in great anger insulted and humiliated Facheng, and Facheng in resentment and grievance hanged himself and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuzhang inner administrator Qian Facheng came to the princely residence to pay court, Shuling immediately detailed Facheng's son Jiqing to lead horse and arms. Jiqing, mortified, delayed; Shuling flew into a rage and abused Facheng until Facheng, bitter and aggrieved, hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 州縣非其部內，亦徵攝案治之，朝貴及下吏有乖忤者，輒誣奏其罪，陷以重辟。

translations.literal: Counties and prefectures outside his jurisdiction he also summoned and tried; court nobles and lower officials who crossed him he at once falsely memorialized for crimes and trapped them in capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He even hauled in and prosecuted counties and prefectures outside his command; any court noble or petty official who offended him he would falsely denounce and trap in a capital sentence.

sentences.zh: 尋進號雲麾將軍，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced in rank to cloud-banner general and given the additional post of scattered-cavalry regular attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to cloud-banner general with the added title of scattered-cavalry regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 三年，加侍中。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was given the additional post of palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was also made palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷都督湘衡桂武四州諸軍事、平南將軍、湘州刺史，侍中、使持節如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was transferred to command all military affairs in Xiang, Heng, Gui, and Wu provinces, made general who pacifies the south and inspector of Xiang; palace attendant and credential staff were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he was moved to command Xiang, Heng, Gui, and Wu, made general who pacifies the south and inspector of Xiang, while retaining palace attendant and the credential staff.

sentences.zh: 諸州鎮聞其至，皆震恐股慄。

translations.literal: When the garrisons of the provinces heard he was coming, all trembled in terror, their legs shaking.
translations.idiomatic: Garrisons throughout the provinces shook with terror when they heard he was coming.

sentences.zh: 叔陵日益暴橫，征伐夷獠，所得皆入己，絲毫不以賞賜。

translations.literal: Shuling daily grew more violent and overbearing; in campaigns against the Yi tribesmen everything taken went into his own purse—he never rewarded with the slightest share.
translations.idiomatic: Shuling grew daily more brutal; on campaigns against the Yi he kept every prize for himself and never gave the least reward.

sentences.zh: 徵求役使，無有紀極。

translations.literal: His levies for labor and service had no limit or end.
translations.idiomatic: His demands for labor and corvée knew no bounds.

sentences.zh: 夜常不臥，燒燭達曉，呼召賓客，說民間細事，戲謔無所不為。

translations.literal: At night he often did not lie down; he burned candles until dawn, summoned guests, and spoke of petty matters among the people—jest and banter of every sort.
translations.idiomatic: He seldom slept at night, kept candles burning till dawn, called in guests, and gossiped over village trifles, joking without restraint.

sentences.zh: 性不飲酒，唯多置餚胾，晝夜食噉而已。

translations.literal: By nature he did not drink wine; he only set out many dishes of meat and ate and gnawed day and night.
translations.idiomatic: He did not drink, but heaped the table with meats and ate constantly, day and night.

sentences.zh: 自旦至中，方始寢寐。

translations.literal: Only from dawn to midday did he finally sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Only from morning till noon did he finally sleep.

sentences.zh: 其曹局文案，非呼不得輒自呈。

translations.literal: Documents in his offices—unless summoned, clerks might not present them on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Office papers might not be submitted unless he called for them.

sentences.zh: 笞罪者皆繫獄，動數年不省視。

translations.literal: Those flogged for punishment were all imprisoned; for years on end he often did not look in on them.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone flogged was thrown into prison and often left unvisited for years.

sentences.zh: 瀟、湘以南，皆逼為左右，㙻里殆無遺者。

translations.literal: South of the Xiao and Xiang, he forced all into his personal service; in hamlet after hamlet almost none were left.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Xiao and Xiang he pressed everyone into personal service until the hamlets were nearly emptied.

sentences.zh: 其中脫有逃竄，輒殺其妻子。

translations.literal: If among them any escaped, he at once killed their wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Any who escaped he killed along with their wives and children.

sentences.zh: 州縣無敢上言，高宗弗之知也。

translations.literal: The prefectures and counties dared not report upward; Emperor Gaozong did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials dared not report up the chain, and Emperor Gaozong never learned of it.

sentences.zh: 尋進號鎮南將軍，給鼓吹一部，遷中衛將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to general who guards the south and given a set of martial pipes and drums; he was moved to central guard general.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to general who guards the south with a suite of pipes and drums and transferred to central guard general.

sentences.zh: 九年，除使持節、都督揚徐東揚南豫四州諸軍事、揚州刺史，侍中、將軍、鼓吹如故。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was appointed credential-bearing, commander of all military affairs in Yang, Xu, Eastern Yang, and Southern Yu provinces, and inspector of Yang; palace attendant, general, and pipes and drums were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he received the credential staff, command of Yang, Xu, Eastern Yang, and Southern Yu, and the Yangzhou inspectorate, while keeping palace attendant, his general's rank, and the pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 十年，至都，加扶，給油幢車。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he reached the capital; he was given bearers and an oil-canopy carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 he arrived at the capital and was granted sedan bearers and an oil-canopy carriage.

sentences.zh: 叔陵治在東府，事務多關治省閣，執事之司，承意順旨，即諷上進用之，微致違忤，必抵以大罪，重者至殊死，道路籍籍，皆言其有非常志。

translations.literal: Shuling's administration was at the Eastern Mansion; many affairs passed through the provincial offices. The bureaus in charge, if they followed his intent and bent to his will, he would hint to the throne to employ them; the slightest opposition he would strike with a great crime—the serious cases reaching execution by dismemberment. On the roads the talk was loud that he harbored extraordinary designs.
translations.idiomatic: Shuling governed from the Eastern Mansion and routed much business through the provincial ministries. Offices that flattered him he pushed for imperial appointment; the least resistance brought a capital charge, even dismemberment. Rumors on every road said he nursed treasonous ambition.

sentences.zh: 叔陵脩飾虛名，每入朝，常於車中馬上執卷讀書，高聲長誦，陽陽自若。

translations.literal: Shuling cultivated a false reputation; whenever he entered court he would in carriage or on horseback hold a scroll and read aloud, reciting in a loud voice, composed and self-satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Shuling cultivated a false reputation; entering court he would read aloud from a scroll in his carriage or on his horse, declaiming loudly with an air of ease.

sentences.zh: 歸坐齋中，或自執斧斤為沐猴百戲。

translations.literal: Back in his study he would sometimes himself take hatchet and adze to perform monkey masquerades.
translations.idiomatic: Back in his study he sometimes took up hatchet and adze to play the monkey masquerader.

sentences.zh: 又好遊冢墓間，遇有塋表主名可知者，輒令左右發掘，取其石誌古器，并骸骨肘脛，持為翫弄，藏之庫中。

translations.literal: He also loved to roam among tombs; when he met a mound whose occupant's name could be read on the tablet, he would order his attendants to dig it up, take the stone epitaph and ancient vessels, and even the bones of arm and shin, which he kept as playthings stored in his treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wandering graveyards; whenever a tombstone gave a readable name he had attendants open the mound, seize stone epitaphs and antiquities, even arm and shin bones, and kept them as toys in his storehouse.

sentences.zh: 府內民間少妻處女，微有色貌者，並即逼納。

translations.literal: Among the people within the mansion, young wives and maidens of even slight beauty he at once forced into his harem.
translations.idiomatic: Within the mansion he forced every young wife or maiden of even slight beauty into his bed.

sentences.zh: 十一年，丁所生母彭氏憂去職。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he left office in mourning for his birth mother, Lady Peng.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 he left office to mourn his birth mother, Lady Peng.

sentences.zh: 頃之，起為中衛將軍，使持節、都督、刺史如故。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled as central guard general; credential staff, command, and inspectorate were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as central guard general with the same credential staff, command, and inspectorate.

sentences.zh: 晉世王公貴人，多葬梅嶺，及彭卒，叔陵啟求於梅嶺葬之，乃發故太傅謝安舊墓，棄去安柩，以葬其母。

translations.literal: In Jin times many lords and nobles were buried at Meiling; when Peng died, Shuling memorialized asking to bury her at Meiling. He then opened the old tomb of Grand Tutor Xie An, cast out An's coffin, and buried his mother there.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin many nobles were buried at Meiling; when Peng died Shuling asked to bury her there, opened Grand Tutor Xie An's old tomb, cast out An's coffin, and laid his mother in the grave.

sentences.zh: 初喪之日，偽為哀毀，自稱刺血寫涅槃經，未及十日，乃令庖廚擊鮮，日進甘膳。

translations.literal: On the first day of mourning he feigned grief and ruin, claiming he pricked his blood to copy the Nirvana Sutra; before ten days had passed he ordered the kitchen to slaughter fresh meat and daily sent rich delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of mourning he faked grief, claiming he copied the Nirvana Sutra in his own blood; within ten days he had the kitchen serve fresh slaughter and daily delicacies.

sentences.zh: 又私召左右妻女，與之姦合，所作尤不軌，侵淫上聞。

translations.literal: He also secretly summoned the wives and daughters of his attendants and fornicated with them; his conduct was especially beyond the bounds, and the offense reached the emperor's ears.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly summoned attendants' wives and daughters and lay with them; his conduct was utterly lawless, and word reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 高宗譴責御史中丞王政，以不舉奏免政官，又黜其典籤親事，仍加鞭捶。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong reprimanded censor-in-chief Wang Zheng for failing to memorialize and report, removed Zheng from office, also dismissed his recorder and personal attendant, and still added flogging.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong rebuked censor-in-chief Wang Zheng for not reporting him, stripped Zheng of office, dismissed his recorder and personal staff, and had them flogged besides.

sentences.zh: 高宗素愛叔陵，不繩之以法，但責讓而已。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong had long loved Shuling and did not bind him with law, but only reproved him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong had long favored Shuling and would not restrain him by law, only scold him.

sentences.zh: 服闋，又為侍中、中軍大將軍。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he again became palace attendant and grand general of the central army.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he again became palace attendant and grand general of the central army.

sentences.zh: 及高宗不豫，太子諸王並入侍疾。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong fell ill, the crown prince and all the princes entered to attend the sickness.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong fell ill, the crown prince and all princes came in to attend him.

sentences.zh: 高宗崩于宣福殿，翌日旦，後主哀頓俯伏，叔陵以剉藥刀斫後主中項。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong died in the Hall of Extending Blessings; on the morrow at dawn, as the Last Ruler in grief collapsed prostrate, Shuling with a medicine-grinding knife hacked the Last Ruler in the nape of the neck.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong died in the Hall of Extending Blessings; at dawn the next day, as the Last Ruler lay prostrate in grief, Shuling struck him in the back of the neck with a medicine knife.

sentences.zh: 太后馳來救焉，叔陵又斫太后數下。

translations.literal: The empress dowager rushed to save him; Shuling also hacked the empress dowager several times.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager rushed to save him; Shuling hacked her several times as well.

sentences.zh: 後主乳媼吳氏，時在太后側，自後掣其肘，後主因得起。

translations.literal: The Last Ruler's wet nurse, Lady Wu, was then at the empress dowager's side; from behind she pulled his elbow, and the Last Ruler was thereby able to rise.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Ruler's wet nurse, Lady Wu, stood beside the empress dowager and pulled his elbow from behind, so the Last Ruler was able to rise.

sentences.zh: 叔陵仍持後主衣，後主自奮得免。

translations.literal: Shuling still held the Last Ruler's garment; the Last Ruler by struggling broke free.
translations.idiomatic: Shuling still clutched the Last Ruler's robe, but the Last Ruler wrenched free.

sentences.zh: 長沙王叔堅手搤叔陵，奪去其刀，仍牽就柱，以其褶袖縛之。

translations.literal: Prince of Changsha Chen Shujian seized Shuling by hand, wrested away his knife, and still dragged him to a pillar and bound him with the sleeve of his robe.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Changsha Chen Shujian grappled Shuling, snatched away his knife, dragged him to a pillar, and bound him with his own robe sleeve.

sentences.zh: 時吳媼已扶後主避賊，叔堅求後主所在，將受命焉。

translations.literal: By then Lady Wu had already helped the Last Ruler flee the assailant; Shujian sought where the Last Ruler was, intending to receive his command.
translations.idiomatic: By then Lady Wu had helped the Last Ruler escape; Shujian looked for the Last Ruler to receive orders.

sentences.zh: 叔陵因奮袖得脫，突走出雲龍門，馳車還東府，呼其甲士，散金銀以賞賜，外召諸王將帥，莫有應者，唯新安王伯固聞而赴之。

translations.literal: Shuling then by flinging his sleeve broke free, burst out through the Cloud Dragon Gate, galloped in his carriage back to the Eastern Mansion, called up his armored men, scattered gold and silver as reward, and summoned the princes and generals from outside—but none responded except Prince of Xin'an Chen Bogu, who on hearing came to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Shuling shook free his sleeve, bolted out the Cloud Dragon Gate, raced to the Eastern Mansion, rallied his guards, scattered gold and silver as bounty, and called the princes and generals—but only Prince of Xin'an Chen Bogu came when he heard.

sentences.zh: 叔陵聚兵僅千人，初欲據城保守，俄而右衛將軍蕭摩訶將兵至府西門，叔陵事急惶恐，乃遣記室韋諒送其鼓吹與摩訶，仍謂之曰：「如其事捷，必以公為台鼎。

translations.literal: Shuling gathered troops of barely a thousand; at first he intended to hold the city and defend, but soon right guard general Xiao Mohe led troops to the western gate of the mansion; Shuling, the affair urgent, in panic and fear sent recorder Wei Liang to present his pipes and drums to Mohe, and still told him: "If the affair succeeds, you will certainly be made one of the highest ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Shuling mustered barely a thousand men and at first meant to hold the city, but right guard Xiao Mohe soon brought troops to the mansion's western gate. In panic Shuling sent staff recorder Wei Liang with his pipes and drums and promised, "If we win, you will sit among the highest ministers."

sentences.zh: 」摩訶紿報之，曰「須王心膂節將自來，方敢從命」。

translations.literal: Mohe deceived him in reply, saying, "I must wait until Your Highness's trusted backbone commanders come in person before I dare obey the command."
translations.idiomatic: Mohe lied in answer: "I must wait until Your Highness's own trusted commanders come before I dare obey."

sentences.zh: 叔陵即遣戴溫、譚騏驎二人詣摩訶所，摩訶執以送臺，斬於閣道下。

translations.literal: Shuling at once sent Dai Wen and Tan Qilin, two men, to Mohe's camp; Mohe seized them and sent them to the tribunal; they were beheaded beneath the covered way.
translations.idiomatic: Shuling sent Dai Wen and Tan Qilin to Mohe's camp; Mohe seized them, sent them to the tribunal, and they were beheaded under the gallery.

sentences.zh: 叔陵自知不濟，遂入內沈其妃張氏及寵妾七人于井中。

translations.literal: Shuling knew himself beyond saving; he then entered the inner quarters and drowned his consort Lady Zhang and seven favored concubines in a well.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing all was lost, Shuling went inside and drowned his consort Lady Zhang and seven favored concubines in a well.

sentences.zh: 叔陵有部下兵先在新林，於是率人馬數百，自小航渡，欲趨新林，以舟艦入北。

translations.literal: Shuling had subordinate troops earlier at Xinlin; he then led several hundred horse and foot, crossed from the small ferry, and intended to hurry to Xinlin and enter the north by warship.
translations.idiomatic: Some of his men were already at Xinlin; he led several hundred horse and foot across the small ferry, meaning to reach Xinlin and flee north by ship.

sentences.zh: 行至白楊路，為臺軍所邀，伯固見兵至，旋避入巷，叔陵馳騎拔刃追之，伯固復還。

translations.literal: When they reached Baiyang Road they were intercepted by the court army; Bogu, seeing troops arrive, at once dodged into a lane; Shuling spurred his horse, drew his blade, and pursued; Bogu came back again.
translations.idiomatic: At Baiyang Road the court army blocked them; Bogu, seeing soldiers, slipped into an alley; Shuling spurred after him with blade drawn, and Bogu returned.

sentences.zh: 叔陵部下，多棄甲潰散，摩訶馬

translations.literal: Shuling's followers for the most part cast off armor and scattered; Mohe's horse
translations.idiomatic: Shuling's men mostly threw off armor and fled; Mohe on horseback

translations.literal: Collation variant: (guest).
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (guest).

sentences.zh: 〔容〕陳智深迎刺叔陵，[1]僵斃于地，閹豎王飛禽抽刀斫之十數下，馬

translations.literal: Collation variant: (Rong); adopted reading: Chen Zhishen came forward to stab Shuling. Editorial footnote marker 1. He stiffened and fell dead on the ground; the eunuch Wang Feiqin drew his blade and hacked him more than ten times; horse
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (Rong); adopted reading: Chen Zhishen came forward to stab Shuling. [1] He stiffened and fell dead; the eunuch Wang Feiqin drew his blade and hacked him more than ten times; on horseback

translations.literal: Collation variant: (guest).
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (guest).

sentences.zh: 〔容〕陳仲華就斬其首，送于臺。

translations.literal: Collation variant: (Rong); adopted reading: Chen Zhonghua then cut off his head and sent it to the tribunal.
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (Rong); adopted reading: Chen Zhonghua then cut off his head and sent it to the tribunal.

sentences.zh: 自寅至巳乃定。

translations.literal: From the hour yin to the hour si order was restored.
translations.idiomatic: From dawn till mid-morning order was restored.

sentences.zh: 尚書八座奏曰：「逆賊故侍中、中軍大將軍、始興王叔陵，幼而很戾，長肆貪虐。

translations.literal: The eight seats of the Secretariat memorialized: "The rebel traitor, the late palace attendant and grand general of the central army, Prince of Shixing Chen Shuling, was perverse in youth and in age indulged greed and cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: The eight secretariat ministers memorialized: "The traitor, the late palace attendant and grand general of the central army, Prince of Shixing Chen Shuling, was savage from childhood and in manhood wallowed in greed and cruelty.

sentences.zh: 出撫湘南，及鎮九水，兩藩甿庶，掃地無遺。

translations.literal: Sent out to pacify south of Xiang and when he held the Nine Waters, in both jurisdictions the common people were swept clean, none left.
translations.idiomatic: As governor south of Xiang and later on the Nine Waters, he left both regions' common folk swept bare.

sentences.zh: 蜂目豺聲，狎近輕薄，不孝不仁，阻兵安忍，無禮無義，唯戮是聞。

translations.literal: Bee eyes and jackal voice, intimate with the frivolous; unfilial and unkind, he relied on arms and was cruel by nature; without rites and without righteousness—only slaughter was heard of him.
translations.idiomatic: With bee eyes and jackal voice he consorted with the worthless; unfilial, unkind, he trusted to arms and delighted in cruelty; without rite or right, only killing followed his name.

sentences.zh: 及居偏憂，婬樂自恣，產子就館，日月相接。

translations.literal: When he dwelt in partial mourning, he gave himself to lust and pleasure; sons born, he lodged them in guest houses—day and night in succession.
translations.idiomatic: During his mother's mourning he abandoned himself to lust; when sons were born he lodged them in guest quarters, one birth after another without pause.

sentences.zh: 晝伏夜遊，恆習姦詭，抄掠居民，歷發丘墓。

translations.literal: By day he hid, by night he roamed, constantly practicing treachery and deceit, plundering the people, repeatedly opening tombs.
translations.idiomatic: He hid by day and prowled by night, ever scheming, plundering townsfolk and opening grave after grave.

sentences.zh: 謝太傅晉朝佐命，草創江左，斲棺露骸，事驚聽視。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Xie aided Jin in founding the mandate and helped create the southeast; to chop open the coffin and expose the bones shocked every ear and eye.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Xie had aided Jin in founding the realm and shaping the southeast; to break open his coffin and bare his bones horrified all who heard.

sentences.zh: 自大行皇帝寢疾，翌日未瘳，叔陵以貴介之地，參侍醫藥，外無戚容，內懷逆弒。

translations.literal: From the time the late emperor took to his sickbed, on the morrow he did not recover; Shuling, in a position of high honor, attended the medicines—outwardly without grief, inwardly harboring regicide.
translations.idiomatic: From the day the late emperor fell ill, by the morrow he had not recovered; Shuling, in honored rank at the bedside, showed no sorrow outwardly while nursing regicide within.

sentences.zh: 大漸之後，聖躬號擗，遂因匍匐，手犯乘輿。

translations.literal: After the final decline, as the sacred person wailed and beat his breast, he took advantage of prostration and with his hand violated the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was failing, as the sacred person wailed and beat his breast, Shuling used the prostration to lay hands on the imperial person.

sentences.zh: 皇太后奉臨，又加鋒刃，窮凶極逆，曠古未儔。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager came in person, he again added the blade; utterly vicious, extreme in treason—unmatched since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager came in person he struck her again; such extreme villainy had no parallel in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 賴長沙王叔堅誠孝懇至，英果奮發，手加挫拉，身蔽聖躬。

translations.literal: Thanks to Prince of Changsha Chen Shujian, whose filial devotion was earnest to the utmost and whose heroic resolve flared up, who with his hands seized and crushed him and with his body shielded the sacred person.
translations.idiomatic: Only Prince of Changsha Chen Shujian, utterly earnest in loyalty, seized him with his own hands and shielded the emperor with his body.

sentences.zh: 叔陵仍奔東城，招集凶黨，餘毒方熾，自害妻孥。

translations.literal: Shuling still fled to the eastern city, gathered vicious partisans—the poison not yet spent—and killed his wife and children himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shuling still fled to the eastern quarter, rallied his ruffians, and even murdered his own wife and children.

sentences.zh: 雖應時梟懸，猶未攄憤怨，臣等參議，請依宋代故事，流尸中江，汙潴其室，并毀其所生彭氏墳廟，還謝氏之塋。

translations.literal: Though in due time he was beheaded and hung up, our indignant grief is not yet vented; we your subjects jointly deliberate and ask, following the Song dynasty precedent, to float the corpse in the middle of the river, befoul his dwelling with filth, and also destroy the tombs and temples of his birth mother Lady Peng and restore the mound of the Xie clan."
translations.idiomatic: Though he was promptly beheaded, our rage is not spent. We jointly ask, as in Song precedent, to cast his corpse into mid-river, befoul his house, destroy his mother Lady Peng's tomb and shrine, and restore the Xie burial mound."

sentences.zh: 」制曰：「凶逆梟獍，反噬宮闈，賴宗廟之靈，時從仆滅。

translations.literal: " The edict said: "The vicious traitor, owl and cur, turned to bite the palace apartments; thanks to the imperial ancestors' spirits, he was quickly cut down.
translations.idiomatic: "The edict read: "The traitor, more beast than man, turned to savage the inner palace; thanks to the imperial ancestors' spirits he was swiftly destroyed.

sentences.zh: [2]撫情語事，酸憤兼懷，朝議有章，宜從所奏也。」

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 2. When I consider the matter with feeling and speak to the facts, bitterness and indignation are both in my breast; the court deliberation has proper regulations—it is fitting to follow what was memorialized."
translations.idiomatic: [2] Considering the matter in grief and speaking to the facts, bitterness and indignation fill my breast; the court's deliberation is in order, and it is fitting to follow what was memorialized."

sentences.zh: 叔陵諸子，即日並賜死。

translations.literal: Shuling's sons, that same day, were all granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Shuling's sons were all ordered to die that same day.

sentences.zh: 前衡陽內史彭暠、諮議參軍兼記室鄭信、中錄事參軍兼記室韋諒、典籤俞公喜，並伏誅。

translations.literal: Former Hengyang inner administrator Peng Hao, deliberation staff officer and concurrent recorder Zheng Xin, central recorder staff officer and concurrent recorder Wei Liang, and recorder Yu Gongxi were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Former Hengyang inner administrator Peng Hao, deliberation officer and recorder Zheng Xin, central recorder and recorder Wei Liang, and recorder Yu Gongxi were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 暠，叔陵舅也，初隨高宗在關中，頗有勤效，因藉叔陵將領歷陽、衡陽二郡。

translations.literal: Hao was Shuling's maternal uncle; he had early followed Emperor Gaozong in Guanzhong and had considerable merit, and through Shuling's patronage commanded troops and held Liyang and Hengyang, two commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was Shuling's uncle on his mother's side; he had followed Emperor Gaozong in Guanzhong with some merit and, through Shuling's favor, held command over Liyang and Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 信以便書記，有寵，謀謨皆預焉。

translations.literal: Xin, because he was skilled in shorthand, was favored; in planning and counsel he had a part in everything.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was skilled at shorthand and enjoyed favor; he took part in every plan.

sentences.zh: 諒，京兆人，梁侍中、護軍將軍粲之子也，以學業為叔陵所引。

translations.literal: Liang was a native of Jingzhao, son of Liang attendant-in-ordinary and protector-general Can; he was brought in by Shuling for his learning.
translations.idiomatic: Liang came from Jingzhao, son of Liang attendant-in-ordinary and protector-general Can, and was recruited by Shuling for his scholarship.

sentences.zh: 陳智深以誅叔陵之功為巴陵內史，封游安縣子。

translations.literal: Chen Zhishen, for merit in executing Shuling, was made inner administrator of Baling and enfeoffed as Viscount of You'an.
translations.idiomatic: For killing Shuling, Chen Zhishen was made inner administrator of Baling and enfeoffed as Viscount of You'an.

sentences.zh: 陳仲華為下嶲太守，封新夷縣子。

translations.literal: Chen Zhonghua was made administrator of Xia Gui and enfeoffed as Viscount of Xinyi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhonghua was made administrator of Xia Gui and enfeoffed as Viscount of Xinyi.

sentences.zh: 王飛禽除伏波將軍。

translations.literal: Wang Feiqin was appointed general who crosses the waves.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Feiqin was made general who crosses the waves.

sentences.zh: [3]賜金各有差。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 3. Gold was bestowed to each in differing amounts.
translations.idiomatic: [3] Gold was bestowed in differing amounts to each.

sentences.zh: 新安王伯固

translations.literal: Prince of Xin'an Chen Bogu
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xin'an Chen Bogu

sentences.zh: 新安王伯固字牢之，世祖之第五子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Xin'an Chen Bogu, styled Laozhi, was the fifth son of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xin'an Chen Bogu, styled Laozhi, was Emperor Wen's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 生而龜胸，目通精揚白，形狀眇小，而俊辯善言論。

translations.literal: From birth he had a pigeon chest; his eyes were clear with the whites showing; his form was slight and small, yet he was handsome in debate and skilled in discourse.
translations.idiomatic: He was born with a pigeon chest and eyes whose whites showed bright; though slight in stature he was handsome in debate and fluent in speech.

sentences.zh: 天嘉六年，立為新安郡王，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianchen, he was established as Prince of Xin'an with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianchen year 6 he was made Prince of Xin'an with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 廢帝嗣立，為使持節、都督南琅邪彭城東海三郡諸軍事、雲麾將軍、彭城琅邪二郡太守。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor succeeded, he was made credential-bearing, commander of all military affairs in southern Langye, Pengcheng, and Donghai, cloud-banner general, and administrator of Pengcheng and Langye.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor succeeded, he received the credential staff, command of southern Langye, Pengcheng, and Donghai, the rank of cloud-banner general, and the Pengcheng and Langye administratorates.

sentences.zh: 尋入為丹陽尹，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Soon he entered court as governor of Danyang; his general's rank was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he entered court as governor of Danyang, keeping his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 太建元年，進號智武將軍，尹如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taijian, he was advanced to general of intelligent martiality; his governorship was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 1 he was promoted to general of intelligent martiality while keeping the Danyang post.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，進號翊右將軍。

translations.literal: When his term ended, he was advanced to general who assists the right.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he was promoted to general who assists the right.

sentences.zh: 尋授使持節、都督吳興諸軍事、平東將軍、吳興太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the credential staff, made area commander of all military affairs in Wuxing, Pacify-the-East General, and Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he received the credential staff and was made area commander of Wuxing military affairs, Pacify-the-East general, and administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 四年，入為侍中、翊前將軍，遷安前將軍、中領軍。

translations.literal: In year 4 he entered the capital as Palace Attendant and Forward Aide General; he was moved to Pacify-the-Front General and Central Army Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he entered the capital as palace attendant and forward aide general, then became pacify-the-front general and central army inspector.

sentences.zh: 七年，出為使持節、散騎常侍、都督南徐南豫南北兗四州諸軍事、鎮北將軍、南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In year 7 he went out with the credential staff as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, area commander of all military affairs in the four provinces South Xu, South Yu, North Xu, and North Yan, Pacify-the-North General, and Inspector of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he went out bearing the credential staff as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, area commander of South Xu, South Yu, North Xu, and North Yan, pacify-the-north general, and inspector of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 伯固性嗜酒，而不好積聚，所得祿俸，用度無節，酣醉以後，多所乞丐，於諸王之中，最為貧窶，高宗每矜之，特加賞賜。

translations.literal: Bogu by nature loved wine and did not like to hoard; the salary he received was spent without measure; after deep drunkenness he often begged from others; among all the princes he was poorest, and Emperor Gaozong often pitied him and gave him special rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Bogu loved wine and would not save; his salary vanished without plan, and when drunk he often begged from others. Among the princes he was the poorest, and Emperor Gaozong often pitied him and gave special gifts.

sentences.zh: 伯固雅性輕率，好行鞭捶，在州不知政事，日出田獵，或乘眠轝至於草間，輒呼民下從遊，動至旬日，所捕獐鹿，多使生致，高宗頗知之，遣使責讓者數矣。

translations.literal: Bogu's natural disposition was frivolous; he liked to wield the whip; in the province he paid no heed to government affairs; by day he went out hunting, sometimes riding a sleeping litter into the grass, then calling commoners to follow his excursions—often for ten days at a stretch; the deer and boar he caught he mostly had brought in alive; Emperor Gaozong knew of this fairly well and several times sent envoys to rebuke him.
translations.idiomatic: Bogu was frivolous by nature and fond of the whip. In his province he ignored government, hunted by day, sometimes rode a sleeping litter into the meadows, and called commoners to join him for outings that could last ten days. The deer and boar he took he mostly had brought in alive. Emperor Gaozong knew of it and sent envoys to rebuke him more than once.

sentences.zh: 十年，入朝，又為侍中、鎮右將軍，尋除護軍將軍。

translations.literal: In year 10 he came to court and again became Palace Attendant and Pacify-the-Right General; soon he was made Protector of the Army General.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 he came to court and again became palace attendant and pacify-the-right general; soon he was made protector of the army general.

sentences.zh: 其年，為國子祭酒，領左驍騎將軍，侍中、鎮右並如故。

translations.literal: That year he was made libationer of the National University and concurrently led the Left Valiant Cavalry; Palace Attendant and Pacify-the-Right remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was made libationer of the National University and concurrently led the left valiant cavalry; palace attendant and pacify-the-right remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 伯固頗知玄理，而墮業無所通，至於擿句問難，往往有奇意。

translations.literal: Bogu was fairly versed in arcane principle, yet in his studies he mastered nothing; when it came to posing lines and challenging with questions, he often had striking ideas.
translations.idiomatic: Bogu knew something of arcane learning yet mastered no art; when he posed lines and pressed others in debate, he often showed a striking turn of mind.

sentences.zh: 為政嚴苛，國學有墮遊不脩習者，重加檟楚，生徒懼焉，由是學業頗進。

translations.literal: In governing he was harsh and exacting; in the National University there were idle wanderers who did not pursue their studies—he heavily flogged them with the cudgel; the students feared him, and thereby learning advanced considerably.
translations.idiomatic: As an administrator he was harsh. Students in the National University who idled instead of studying he beat heavily with the cudgel; they feared him, and study thereafter advanced sharply.

sentences.zh: 十二年，領宗正卿。

translations.literal: In year 12 he concurrently held Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 he also held director of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 十三年，為使持節、都督揚南徐東揚南豫四州諸軍事、揚州刺史，侍中、將軍如故。

translations.literal: In year 13 he was made credential-bearing, area commander of all military affairs in the four provinces Yang, South Xu, East Yang, and South Yu, and Inspector of Yangzhou; Palace Attendant and general remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 he was made credential-bearing area commander of Yang, South Xu, East Yang, and South Yu and inspector of Yangzhou; palace attendant and general remained as before.

sentences.zh: 後主初在東宮，與伯固甚相親狎，伯固又善嘲謔，高宗每宴集，多引之。

translations.literal: When the Last Ruler was first in the Eastern Palace, he and Bogu were very intimate; Bogu was also skilled at banter and raillery; whenever Emperor Gaozong held a feast, he often had him brought in.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Ruler was still crown prince in the Eastern Palace, he and Bogu were very close. Bogu was also skilled at banter, and Emperor Gaozong often summoned him to feasts.

sentences.zh: 叔陵在江州，心害其寵，陰求疵瑕，將中之以法。

translations.literal: Shuling was in Jiangzhou and inwardly resented Bogu's favor; he secretly sought flaws and intended to strike him down by law.
translations.idiomatic: Shuling was in Jiangzhou and resented Bogu's favor; he secretly looked for faults and meant to bring him down by law.

sentences.zh: 及叔陵入朝，伯固懼罪，諂求其意，乃共訕毀朝賢，歷詆文武，雖耆年高位，皆面折之，無所畏忌。

translations.literal: When Shuling entered court, Bogu feared punishment and fawned to learn his intent; thereupon together they slandered court worthies, reviling in turn civil and military men—even elders of years and high rank they confronted to their faces, fearing nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuling came to court, Bogu feared punishment and fawned on him to learn his mind; together they slandered court worthies and abused civil and military men in turn—even elders of years and high rank they confronted to the face without fear.

sentences.zh: 伯固性好射雉，叔陵又好開發冢墓，出遊野外，必與偕行，於是情好大協，遂謀不軌。

translations.literal: Bogu by nature loved shooting pheasants; Shuling also loved opening and rifling tombs; when they went out into the wilds they always went together; their feelings therefore greatly harmonized, and they plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Bogu loved shooting pheasants and Shuling loved opening tombs; abroad in the wilds they always went together, their feelings matched, and they plotted treason.

sentences.zh: 伯固侍禁中，每有密語，必報叔陵。

translations.literal: Bogu attended within the forbidden quarters; whenever there was a secret word, he always reported it to Shuling.
translations.idiomatic: Bogu attended within the palace; whenever there was a secret word he reported it to Shuling.

sentences.zh: 及叔陵出奔東府，遣使告之，伯固單馬馳赴，助叔陵指揮。

translations.literal: When Shuling fled to the Eastern Palace, he sent a messenger to tell Bogu; Bogu rode alone at full speed to join him and helped Shuling direct operations.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuling fled to the Eastern Palace he sent word to Bogu; Bogu rode alone at full speed to join him and helped direct the fighting.

sentences.zh: 知事不捷，便欲遁走，會四門已閉不得出，因同趣白楊道。

translations.literal: Knowing affairs would not succeed, he wished to flee; it happened that the four gates were already shut and he could not get out, so together they made for Baimang Road.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the cause was lost, he meant to flee; the four gates were already shut and he could not leave, so together they made for Baimang Road.

sentences.zh: 臺馬

translations.literal: Platform horse
translations.idiomatic: Platform horse

translations.literal: (guest)
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (guest).

sentences.zh: 〔容〕至，為亂兵所殺，尸於東昌館門，時年二十八。

translations.literal: [Rong] arrived; he was killed by mutinous troops; his corpse lay at the gate of the Dongchang hostel; he was twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: [Rong] arrived; mutinous troops killed him; his body lay at the gate of the Dongchang hostel; he was twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「伯固同茲悖逆，殞身途路。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Bogu shared in this rebellion and perished on the road.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Bogu shared in this rebellion and perished on the road.

sentences.zh: 今依外議，意猶弗忍，可特許以庶人禮葬。

translations.literal: Now, following outside opinion, our mind still cannot bear it; he may specially be allowed burial with commoner rites.
translations.idiomatic: Following outside opinion, our mind still cannot bear it; he may be buried with commoner rites as a special grace.

sentences.zh: 」又詔曰：「伯固隨同巨逆，自絕于天，俾無遺育，抑有恆典。

translations.literal: " Another edict said: "Bogu followed the great rebel and cut himself off from Heaven; to leave no descendants is the constant statute.
translations.idiomatic: " Another edict said, "Bogu followed the great rebel and cut himself off from Heaven; to leave no descendants is the constant statute.

sentences.zh: 但童孺靡識，兼預葭莩，寘之甸人，良以惻憫，及伯固所生王氏，[4]可並特宥為庶人。

translations.literal: Yet children know nothing and also share the reed-and-rush tie; to place them among field folk is truly from compassion; and Wang, who bore Bogu, Editorial footnote marker 4. may both be specially pardoned as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the children know nothing and share the family tie; to set them among common folk is true compassion; and Wang, who bore Bogu, [4] may both be specially pardoned as commoners.

sentences.zh: 」國除。

translations.literal: The state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：孔子稱「富與貴，是人之所欲，非其道得之，不處也」。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Confucius said, "Wealth and honor are what men desire; if not obtained by the proper way, one does not dwell in them."
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Confucius said, "Wealth and honor are what men desire; if not obtained by the proper way, one does not dwell in them."

sentences.zh: 上自帝王，至于黎獻，莫不嫡庶有差，長幼攸序。

translations.literal: From emperors and kings down to the common multitude, none lacks distinction between principal wife and concubine, or order between elder and younger.
translations.idiomatic: From emperors and kings down to the common multitude, none lacks distinction between principal wife and concubine or order between elder and younger.

sentences.zh: 叔陵險躁奔競，遂行悖逆，轘磔形骸，未臻其罪，汙潴居處，不足彰過，悲哉。

translations.literal: Shuling was dangerous, restless, and driven to outstrip others; he then carried out rebellion; sundering his body by the cart-wheel did not reach his crime; defiling pools at his dwelling did not suffice to show his fault—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Shuling was dangerous, restless, and driven to outstrip others, then carried out rebellion. Sundering his body by the cart-wheel did not reach his crime; defiling pools at his dwelling did not suffice to show his fault—alas!

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 摩訶馬

translations.literal: Mohe horse
translations.idiomatic: On "Mohe horse"

translations.literal: (guest)
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (guest).

sentences.zh: 〔容〕陳智深迎刺叔陵 據《南史》改，下同。

translations.literal: [Rong] Chen Zhishen intercepted and stabbed Shuling—emended according to the Southern History; the same below.
translations.idiomatic: On "[Rong] Chen Zhishen intercepted and stabbed Shuling": emended per the Southern History; the same below.

sentences.zh: 按《通鑑》亦作「馬容」，胡注云：「行軍，擇便於鞍馬、軀幹壯偉者，乘馬居前，以壯軍容，謂之馬容。」

translations.literal: Note: the Comprehensive Mirror also reads "Ma Rong"; Hu's note says: "On campaign, men chosen for ease in the saddle and stout of frame ride horses at the fore to enhance the army's bearing—they are called Ma Rong."
translations.idiomatic: The Comprehensive Mirror also reads Ma Rong; Hu's note says that on campaign men chosen for ease in the saddle and stout frame ride ahead to enhance the army's bearing and are called Ma Rong.

sentences.zh: 時從仆滅 「仆」南監本作「釋」，北監本、殿本作「殄」。

translations.literal: At that time the followers were destroyed "followers" in the Southern Supervisory edition reads "released"; the Northern Supervisory, Hall, and Palace editions read "exterminated."
translations.idiomatic: On "at that time the followers were destroyed": followers in the Southern Supervisory edition reads released; the Northern Supervisory, Hall, and Palace editions read exterminated.

sentences.zh: 汲本亦作「殄」，下有小注云一作「釋」。

translations.literal: The Ji edition also reads "exterminated," with a small note below that one reading is "released."
translations.idiomatic: The Ji edition also reads exterminated, with a small note that one reading is released.
